verification.semanticRedEvidence: Author evidence reports assertion-failure REDs for C owner partial preservation, lexical alias, .markdown publication, changed-copy replay, missing imported graph edges, and integrated C intent fault. These are behavior assertions using real files, SQLite, and the owner worker, rather than setup failures.

assessment: The integrated A→B→C→A case exercises C intent rename, document rename, post-publication, lost ACK after owner commit, and cancellation after B ACK. It checks partial counts, B copy and identity preservation, C retry convergence to one identity/revision/intent acceptance, and safe private-intent state. Separate S08 tests retain broader publisher fault coverage.

An owner failure after a changed copy publishes leaves the previous desired revision and the new copy; matching-intent replay advances the same document to revision 2. A different intent cannot bypass the previous-hash guard. Unchanged rerun adds no intent or job, while canonical alias provenance adds no duplicate revision.

The importer performs no ledger or graph writes. It publishes a body-free private intent and contained copy, then sends exactly seven identity/provenance fields to the existing owner. Owner acceptance commits source, alias, document, desired revision, and job; the owner indexing job reads the contained copy for local_import_source while preserving the external source root.

The revised S17 owner-drain fixture proves eventual resolved and missing graph rows for an imported document. The Wave 2 fixture checks that the producer itself does not write graph rows immediately, so the two tests together preserve graph connectivity coverage without introducing a second writer.
The outside-root entry produces no store copy or document row. Settings remains the explicit import trigger; the reviewed diff adds no MCP import or indexing control.
documentedLimits: The C matrix uses a test-only fault hook on the importer instance; production callers do not set it. The S08 suite tests additional individual publisher faults.
S17 verifies representative failure boundaries and focused adjacent regressions; it does not claim a full release or package test run.
